The Indus Waters Treaty, signed in 1960, is a water-sharing agreement between India and Pakistan. Furthermore, it would underscore India's commitment to strategic autonomy, signaling its determination to protect its national interests in the face of evolving global power dynamics.

By revising the treaty, India aims to increase its hydropower generation capacity, reduce its reliance on fossil fuels, and boost its agricultural output. This, in turn, would contribute to India's economic growth, energy security, and food sovereignty.
